original_question: Fix a transitive permutation group G contained in S_n for n >= 3 and a tuple sigma = (sigma_1, ..., sigma_r) of generators of G with product equal to 1. Let H(sigma) be the Hurwitz space over Z that parametrizes tamely ramified degree-n covers f: X -> P^1 having branch cycle description sigma, and let phi_sigma: H(sigma) -> M_g send such a cover to the isomorphism class of X. For a prime p, is H(sigma) tensor F_p nonempty; and if it is nonempty, what is the dimension of the image of phi_sigma tensor F_p?
target_in_paper: Section 1, "Rational functions with given monodromy on generic curves" (Bouw–Wewers), specifically Problem 1.2, with Problem 1.1 as the motivating special case.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's general Hurwitz-space formulation very closely: it fixes a transitive permutation group G ⊂ S_n and a generating tuple σ with product 1; it introduces the corresponding Hurwitz space H(σ); it considers the natural map φ_σ to the moduli space M_g of source curves; and it asks, for a prime p, both about nonemptiness of the characteristic-p fiber and about the dimension of the image in moduli. This is the right level of generality for the paper's Problem 1.2, which abstracts the special A_5, p=2, genus-1 case posed just before it in Problem 1.1.
missing_details: The paper's genus g is not an independent parameter; it is determined by the branch-cycle data σ via the Riemann–Hurwitz formula.
The intended covers are tame in characteristic p, so the prime p must be compatible with the ramification data (equivalently, p must be prime to the ramification indices / orders occurring in σ).
Nonemptiness should be interpreted geometrically: whether the characteristic-p fiber of the relevant Hurwitz space has points over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p.
The paper asks for determination/computation of the image dimension, not merely whether it is positive.
The natural map φ_σ is the forgetful morphism sending a cover f: X → P^1 to the moduli point [X] in the coarse moduli space M_g.

To be fully paper-faithful, one should refer to the Hurwitz space attached to the prescribed branch-cycle data σ, rather than an arbitrary Hurwitz space over Z without noting the tame characteristic-p restriction.
The motivating special case from Problem 1.1 is the tuple of five 3-cycles in A_5 in characteristic 2; that context explains why the general question is being asked.
refined_question: Let σ = (σ_1, ..., σ_r) be a tuple of permutations in S_n whose product is 1 and which generate a transitive subgroup G ⊂ S_n, and let g be the genus determined by σ through the Riemann–Hurwitz formula. Let H_σ denote the Hurwitz space parametrizing degree-n covers f: X → P^1 with branch-cycle description σ, and let φ_σ: H_σ → M_g be the forgetful morphism sending such a cover to the isomorphism class of its source curve X. For a prime p for which this ramification data are tame in characteristic p, determine whether the geometric fiber H_σ ⊗ F_p is nonempty; and, when it is nonempty, determine the dimension of the image of φ_σ ⊗ F_p in M_g ⊗ F_p.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's general Hurwitz-space question, not at the preceding special case alone. In Section 1, Bouw and Wewers first isolate a concrete unresolved case in characteristic 2 (Problem 1.1), and then formulate the broader problem for arbitrary branch-cycle data σ and prime p. Your draft already reproduces that broader setup quite faithfully. The main adjustments needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are: (i) make explicit that the genus g is determined by σ; (ii) record that the question is about tame characteristic-p realizations, so p must be compatible with the ramification data; and (iii) interpret nonemptiness as geometric nonemptiness of the characteristic-p fiber. Those are exactly the hidden assumptions supplied by the surrounding discussion that motivates Problem 1.2 from Problem 1.1.
